headline: WHO urges lifestyle changes over drugs for childhood obesity, new global guidelines state
summary: The WHO's first global guidelines prioritize healthy food, regular physical activity, and counseling for children and adolescents. Weight-loss drugs are suggested only as a last resort for 10-19 year olds, under expert supervision.
details: The World Health Organization (WHO) has released its first global guidelines on childhood and adolescent obesity, emphasizing lifestyle changes over weight-loss medication. The recommendations highlight the importance of healthy eating, regular physical activity, and counseling as primary interventions.

Published yesterday, the guidelines suggest that weight-loss drugs may be considered for individuals aged 10 to 19 years who are struggling with obesity. However, this is only after initial steps involving dietary adjustments, physical activity, and counseling under expert supervision have proven unsuccessful.

UNICEF data indicates a concerning trend: the number of children and adolescents who are overweight or obese has surpassed those who are underweight. Historically, undernutrition was the predominant nutritional issue among this age group.

Luz Maria De Regil, Director of WHO's Nutrition and Food Safety Department, noted that there is currently insufficient evidence regarding the long-term safety and efficacy of weight-loss medications for children. The organization is actively monitoring ongoing research into these drugs.

headline: 3 foreign nationals killed, 36 injured in attacks on two Saudi international airports
summary: Three foreign nationals were killed and 36 others injured in attacks on two international airports in Saudi Arabia on Wednesday and Thursday. The Kingdom has accused Iran-backed Houthi rebels from Yemen of being behind the assaults.
details: Three foreign nationals, including two women, have been killed and at least 36 others injured in attacks on two international airports in Saudi Arabia. The incidents occurred on Wednesday and Thursday, targeting King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and Abha International Airport in Abha.
Saudi Arabia's General Authority of Civil Aviation reported these details, accusing Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi armed group of being responsible for the assaults.
At Abha International Airport, two foreign women were killed; one was a Moroccan national and the other an Algerian. This attack also left 28 people injured.
Separately, at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, one Sudanese national was killed. Eight people were injured in this incident, including five Saudi citizens.
The exact timing of each attack was not specified in the statement, only that they occurred on Wednesday and Thursday. The Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) has condemned the attacks.

The US Embassy in Riyadh has issued a special travel warning for American citizens in Saudi Arabia, citing the critical situation surrounding the ongoing Saudi-led coalition operations against Houthis in Yemen and these international airport attacks.
